annotation.title_clean: Regulation (EU) 2017/746 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 April 2017 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices and repealing Directive 98/79/EC and Commission Decision 2010/227/EU
annotation.title_en: Regulation (EU) 2017/746 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices and repealing Directive 98/79/EC and Commission Decision 2010/227/EU
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union L 117/176
annotation.summary_en: The EU In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices Regulation (IVDR) sets out a risk-based framework for placing IVD devices, including standalone software, on the EU market. It covers four risk classes (A–D), conformity assessment by notified bodies, CE marking, UDI traceability, the Eudamed database, performance studies, post-market surveillance, vigilance and manufacturer liability coverage. It contains no AI or robotics provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Four risk classes (A-D) with notified-body involvement required for classes B, C and D
Software intended for medical diagnostic purposes qualifies as an IVD device
Manufacturers must maintain risk management, quality management and post-market surveillance systems and report serious incidents
UDI system and Eudamed database for traceability and transparency
Manufacturers must have financial coverage for liability under Directive 85/374/EEC; authorised representatives jointly and severally liable
